items.question: A cyclist rides 54 kilometers in 1.5 hours at a constant speed. What is her average speed in m/s? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Speed-distance-time with km/h to m/s unit conversion.

items.question: A lab technician has 500 mL of a 12% (w/v) salt solution, meaning 12 g of salt per 100 mL of solution. She adds 250 mL of pure water and mixes thoroughly. What is the salt concentration of the resulting solution, in percent (g per 100 mL)? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Dilution percentage: constant solute mass over larger volume.

items.question: An architect builds a scale model of a tower at a ratio of 1:250. The model stands 28 cm tall. How tall is the actual tower, in meters? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Scale ratio applied to model height, then cm-to-m conversion.

items.question: A solid metal cube has edges of 4 cm and a mass of 352 g. What is its density in g/cm3? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Cube volume combined with mass to compute density.

items.question: A 60-watt LED bulb converts only 20% of the electrical energy it consumes into visible light; the remaining 80% leaves the bulb as heat. How much heat energy, in joules, does the bulb produce while running for 30 seconds? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Combines power, time and efficiency split (light vs heat).

items.question: A bacteriologist starts a culture with 250 cells. Under her incubation conditions the population doubles every 20 minutes. Assuming no cell deaths and unlimited nutrients, how many cells are present after exactly 2 hours? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Exponential doubling: converts elapsed time to doubling count, then scales.

items.question: The natural history museum's new animatronic dinosaur is advertised as sprinting at 8 m/s. A visitor stands 96 meters down the hall from it. If the machine charged straight at her at its full advertised speed, how many seconds would it take to reach her? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Same speed-distance-time skill in a playful story framing.

items.question: POSITION LOG (constant velocity assumed): t = 0 s -> x = 12 m; t = 6 s -> x = 54 m. Report the velocity in km/h. Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Velocity from a terse sensor log, then m/s to km/h conversion.

items.question: A projectile is launched at 21 m/s at exactly 45 degrees above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance and using g = 9.8 m/s^2, its horizontal range is R = v^2 * sin(2*theta) / g. What is the range in meters? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Projectile range formula (physics) evaluated with trigonometry (math).

items.question: Two resistors, one of 6 ohms and one of 3 ohms, are connected in parallel across an ideal 12-volt battery. What is the total current drawn from the battery, in amperes? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Parallel-resistance algebra combined with Ohm's law.

items.question: Complete combustion of methane follows CH4 + 2 O2 -> CO2 + 2 H2O. Using molar masses of 16 g/mol for CH4 and 44 g/mol for CO2, how many grams of CO2 are produced by burning 8.0 g of methane? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Stoichiometry chain: mass to moles, 1:1 mole ratio, moles to mass.

items.question: A radioactive isotope used in medical imaging has a half-life of 8 days. What percentage of the original activity remains after 40 days? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Exponential decay from half-life (nuclear chemistry) with percentage arithmetic.

items.question: In a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype (genotype aa). What percentage of individuals are heterozygous carriers (Aa)? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Hardy-Weinberg genetics: recessive frequency to q, then 2pq.

items.question: The referenced genetics text reports Mendel's classic result for crossing two heterozygous organisms. In an F2 sample of 1,260 pea plants, how many plants are expected to show the recessive trait? Answer with a plain number.

source_fact.quote: For example, Mendel found that if you cross heterozygous organisms your odds of getting the dominant trait is 3:1.

items.author_note: Retrieves Mendel's 3:1 ratio, then applies proportional statistics to a sample.

items.question: The reference text names the nearest star to Earth apart from the Sun and states its distance in light-years. If a robotic probe travels at exactly one-tenth of the speed of light, how many years would the one-way trip take? (One light-year is the distance light travels in one year; ignore acceleration and deceleration.) Answer with a plain number.

source_fact.quote: The nearest star to the Earth, apart from the Sun, is Proxima Centauri, 4.2465 light-years (40.175 trillion kilometres) away.

items.author_note: Retrieves Proxima Centauri's distance, then applies light-year kinematics at 0.1c.

items.question: A country emits 5.2 gigatonnes of CO2 per year, 60% of which comes from electricity generation. A new policy cuts power-sector emissions by 25% while all other sectors stay flat. What is the country's new total annual emission, in gigatonnes of CO2? Answer with a plain number.
items.author_note: Climate mitigation scenario: sector shares and nested percentage reduction.
